text: Pole position is first place on the starting grid, won by the fastest lap in the timed session before the race.
Qualifying is the timed session before the race; the fastest laps decide the starting order.
A stint is one run on one set of tyres, between pit stops.
A compound is a type of tyre: the soft is fastest but wears quickest, the hard lasts longest.
Tyre degradation is the time a tyre loses each lap as it wears.
The undercut is pitting before a rival, so fresh tyres gain time while the rival stays out with worn ones.
The pit loss is the time a stop costs: the slow lap into the pits (in-lap) and the lap back out (out-lap).
Track evolution is the track getting faster through a session as rubber builds up on it.
A fuel-corrected lap time has the gain from fuel burning off removed, so laps from full and empty tanks compare fairly.
Telemetry is what the car records many times a second: speed, throttle, brake and gear.
A delta is the time gap between the two drivers at one point on the lap.
